clusters.headline_hint: Mass migration influx into Spanish enclave of Ceuta triggers European crisis and border controls

claims.text: Leaders from 22 of the 27 EU member states signed an open letter demanding an urgent video meeting of interior ministers to coordinate a response to the migrant influx in Ceuta.
Spanish Interior Ministry reported that nearly all of the 60,000 migrants who breached the border into Ceuta since July 29 had departed by August 1.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni posted on X that defending the Union's external borders is a shared European responsibility.
At least 67 people died attempting to reach the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from Morocco during the mass border surge.
Ceuta and Melilla are autonomous Spanish cities on the northern coast of Africa that form the European Union's only land borders on the African mainland.
A Spanish Supreme Court ruling published on July 8 barred Spanish authorities from immediately returning migrants who arrive by sea.
Italy temporarily suspended its Schengen-area border-free agreement with Spain for one month following the migrant surge into Ceuta.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez criticized the Schengen suspension by other EU members as a selfish, polarising, and unlawful reaction.
Spanish Civil Guard officers began laying a 500-metre floating pneumatic barrier along the Tarajal breakwater in Ceuta to stop migrants from swimming into the enclave.
More than 48,000 of the migrants who entered Ceuta returned to Morocco within 48 hours of crossing.
Juan Jesús Vivas, president of Ceuta, stated that several thousand people still need to be returned and that the situation in the enclave has not fully returned to normal.

clusters.headline_hint: Russian missile strikes kill nine in Kyiv as Ukraine sinks Russian ship in Black Sea

claims.text: A overnight Russian missile and drone barrage against Kyiv killed nine people and injured over 30 others on August 1.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Russia launched 35 missiles and 185 attack drones during the attack, with only one of 27 ballistic missiles intercepted.
Ukrainian drone strikes hit three oil refineries in Russia's Bashkortostan region, roughly 1,000 miles from the front lines.
A sanctioned Russian container ship was sunk in the Black Sea following a attack by Ukrainian drones.
Lithuania's embassy in Kyiv sustained damage when Russian missiles struck near the compound.
In Kyiv's Darnytskyi district, seven people were killed and 14 others injured after strikes caused widespread fires.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky appealed on social media that every package of ballistic missile interceptors saves lives.
Russian state nuclear operator Rosatom confirmed that its 100,000-tonne container ship, the Yanina, was sunk 130 miles from Novorossiysk.
US President Donald Trump stated during a Cabinet meeting at Camp David that the US had not yet agreed to allow Ukraine to produce Patriot missiles under license.

clusters.headline_hint: Famed mountaineer Nirmal Purja among climbers killed in Pakistan avalanche

claims.text: Renowned British-Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja and nine other expedition members died in an avalanche on Broad Peak in Pakistan.
Broad Peak in Northern Pakistan is 26,414 feet high, making it the 12th-highest mountain in the world.
In 2019, Nirmal Purja became the first person to climb all 14 world mountains above 8,000 meters in six months and six days.
American mountaineer Mallory Geis, 39, of San Antonio, Texas, was among the climbers killed in the Broad Peak avalanche.
Pakistani rescue officials recovered the bodies of three climbers: Mallory Geis, Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy of Oman, and Pur Bahadur Gurung of Nepal.
Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah expressed shock at the death of six Nepalese and four foreign climbers in the Karakoram range.
Nirmal Purja served in the British military for 16 years, including 10 years in the Special Boat Service, and was awarded an MBE in 2018.

clusters.headline_hint: UEFA and football bodies declare no confidence in FIFA chief Gianni Infantino over World Cup plan

claims.text: FIFA President Gianni Infantino withdrew a proposal to allow private equity investment in a new commercial subsidiary for the World Cup following widespread backlash.
UEFA declared that FIFA leadership under Gianni Infantino had lost the confidence of European football and other governing bodies.
FIFA's scrapped proposal, FIFA Forward Enterprise, aimed to value a new commercial subsidiary at $20 billion and raise up to $4.2 billion from private investors.
CONCACAF issued a statement condemning FIFA's proposal as a unilateral act of poor governance and called for a full review of Infantino's leadership.
Qatar Football Association President Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa bin Ahmed Al Thani applauded Infantino's decision to scrap the plan to prioritize unity among member associations.
Carlos Cordeiro, special adviser to Infantino and senior adviser to the White House Task Force on the 2026 World Cup, resigned amid the backlash.
The Dutch Football Association (KNVB) declared a fundamental breach of trust and stated it no longer has confidence in Gianni Infantino's leadership.

clusters.headline_hint: US embassies urge citizens to leave Middle East amid fears of escalating conflict with Iran

claims.text: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned that any US aggression or regional assistance to US attacks would meet a proportionate, decisive Iranian response.
Kuwait's military stated that its forces destroyed hostile drones launched by Iran targeting government and civilian facilities on Bubiyan Island.
UK Maritime Trade Operations reported that a tanker off Oman was struck by an unknown projectile that damaged its engine room.
US embassies across 10 Middle Eastern countries issued security alerts advising American citizens to consider leaving the region due to potential unforeseen escalation.
Ali Abdollahi, head of Iran's military central command, warned that any country serving as a defensive shield for the US would be engulfed by war.
EUCOM chief Gen. Alexus Grynkewich warned the Pentagon that the US lacks sufficient naval assets to maintain continuous missile defense operations for Israel against Iranian attacks.
US President Donald Trump is considering strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure to force Iran into accepting US ceasefire terms.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps asserted full control over the Strait of Hormuz and declared the waterway closed to traffic without its permission.

clusters.headline_hint: Tourist plane viewing Nazca Lines crashes in Peru, killing 13

claims.text: A tourist sightseeing plane crashed near the Nazca Lines in southern Peru on August 1, killing all 13 people on board.
The crashed aircraft carried 11 passengers and two pilots when it went down in Pueblo Viejo after departing from Pisco.
The aircraft involved in the fatal crash belonged to local Peruvian sightseeing airline Aerodiana.
Local authorities identified the crash victims as seven Italians, two Germans, two Spanish citizens, and two Peruvian crew members.
The Cessna Grand Caravan aircraft crashed at 1:20 pm local time after losing contact with the control tower minutes after departure.
Previous fatal crashes over the Nazca Lines occurred in 2022, 2010, and 2008 due to safety concerns surrounding small tourist flights.

clusters.headline_hint: Political row intensifies over youth protests, police action, and opposition skit in Parliament

claims.text: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke demanded a public apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi over alleged police violence against student protesters during the July 20 march.
Police in Varanasi registered an FIR against Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and MPs Pappu Yadav and Awadhesh Prasad over a skit mocking Ram temple donation theft in Parliament.
BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj filed a police complaint in Delhi against Opposition MPs, accusing them of making a mockery of Sanatan culture during their Parliament protest.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi released a video message stating he forgave students who used abusive language against him during protests at Jantar Mantar, calling them misguided children.
During the protest near Makar Dwar in Parliament, Independent MP Pappu Yadav wore saffron robes and performed a skit portraying a priest stealing money from donation boxes.

clusters.headline_hint: Torrential rain triggers deadly landslides and flooding across Kerala

claims.text: Incessant heavy rain caused flooding and landslips in Kozhikode district, forcing the evacuation of 214 people into eight relief camps.
Authorities in Kozhikode imposed traffic restrictions on heavy and non-essential vehicles along the Thamarassery ghat road due to landslide risks.
Heavy rains and landslides killed at least six people across Kerala, with four deaths occurring in Idukki and Kottayam districts.
The India Meteorological Department issued a red alert forecasting extremely heavy rainfall for eight districts in Kerala, including Pathanamthitta, Idukki, and Kozhikode.
Floodwaters submerged a poultry farm in Pala, Kottayam district, killing approximately 2,500 chickens.
Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan confirmed that 17 houses were completely destroyed and 127 suffered partial damage across the state.
Two people, including a swimming instructor, were reported missing in rain-related incidents in Kannur district.
